slides.kicker: A note from the dad who built it
slides.big: I did not build this because YouTube is bad.
slides.body:
I built it because the feed is. One video turns into forty minutes of whatever holds attention longest, and the parent is the only ending.

So you set the age, the tone, the time of day and how long it runs. We build the playlist to match. When it ends, it ends. No up next, no Shorts, no comments.

The first playlist is free. One child profile. No card. If it does not fit your family, tell me and I will make it better.

slides.kicker: For parents of 3 to 16 year olds

slides.big:
The videos come from YouTube.
The feed around them does not.
slides.hl: The feed around them does not.
slides.body: You set the age, the tone, the time of day and the length. We build the playlist to match. Nothing is recommended. Nothing autoplays that you did not choose.

slides.kicker: Most of the work went into what we left out
list: No data sold to anyone, ever

slides.big:
Calm.
Twenty minutes.
Then it stops.
slides.body: You choose calm, you choose the length. The ending is built in, so you do not have to be the ending.

slides.big: After school is not bedtime. The playlist should not be either.
slides.body: Energetic or calm. Educational or fun. Twenty minutes or forty. Five choices, made by you, before they press play.

slides.big: Is YouTube a rabbit hole in your house?
slides.body:
Blocking is a treadmill. Filters let things through. The problem was never your child's willpower, it is what the feed puts in front of them.

So we built the other way round. You set the shape of the session. We build the playlist. When it ends, it ends.
